newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power edges higher despite mild temps.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power edges higher despite mild temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast edged higher Tuesday as many power marketers returned to the market after the Martin Luther King, Jr. holiday.
"I think some people were caught short yesterday because of the holiday. They had to pay a little higher today for the power," one market source said.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to hover near or slightly above-normal Wednesday through Saturday. Slightly cooler temperatures are forecast for the weekend, Weather Services Corp said.

Firm, peak power prices into the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Wednesday climbed into the $15.00-16.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with the $12.00-13.00 range on Monday.
Firm, off-peak power into TVA was talked at $13.50-14.00, but no deals were confirmed done.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks for Wednesday delivery ranged anywhere from $20.00 to $23.00, with the bulk of the deals reported done around $22.00.
These prices compare with $20.50-21.75 on Monday.
Firm, off-peak power for Wednesday at the Ga./Fla. border was assessed at $14.00 per MWh.

Conversely to the power market, natural gas prices along the Gulf Coast pipes fell by about 25 cents to the $2.90s, pressured by mild temperatures stretching across most of the U.S. and plentiful storage supplies in the East.
Florida Power and Light's 839 megawatt St Lucie 2 nuclear power unit was reduced to 90 percent power for inspections, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported.
Market sources said the power reduction was not having an impact on the market as FP&L was able to meet demand and did not limit availability on its system.
